title: Enterprise privacy evidence outline for security eval
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, evidence-focused brief for AEs and CSEs to use during enterprise security evaluations. It translates technical controls into buyer-facing claims and provides ready-to-send artifact lists, short audit-log language, and objection-handling scripts for SOC2, ISO, and HIPAA-focused RFIs.

How to use this doc:
- For early outbound / discovery: use the 2–3 line evidence statements under "Elevator claims".
- For security calls: share the "Evidence bundle checklist" and use the audit-log snippets as-is in follow-up emails.
- For procurement/Legal: escalate to Solutions Engineering with the "Artifacts to gather" section.

Elevator claims (2–3 lines each):
- SOC2: "Redwood Inference operates under an active SOC2 Type II program covering our hosted and dedicated control planes; we provide a summary of controls and a scoping map that shows which customer-facing services are covered."
- ISO27001: "Our information security management system is aligned to ISO 27001 principles and we publish our ISMS scope and top-level policies for enterprise review; certification plan available on request for private deployments."
- HIPAA: "We offer HIPAA-ready private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and standard BAAs; we segregate PHI at the tenancy level and log access for auditability."

Core data-handling summary (buyer-friendly):
- Data classification: customer inputs routed to isolated model runtimes per-tenant for Dedicated and Private; hosted API uses logical tenancy with RBAC and encryption in transit/end at rest.
- Retention & deletion: configurable retention windows; default short-term caching for inference only. Customers can request retention policy exceptions and evidence of deletion events.
- Key management: KMS integrations (customer-managed keys supported in Private) plus HSM signing for attestation where required.

Audit-log language snippets (paste into RFIs / follow-ups):
- "Audit logging: All inference requests that touch customer-scoped resources are logged with request id, model version, timestamp, calling identity (API key or IAM principal), region, and outcome code. Logs are immutable for the configured retention period and can be exported to customer-owned SIEM via syslog/S3."
- "Access reviews: We provide quarterly access lists for infra and platform roles; ad-hoc export of recent access events available upon request for third-party audit."
- "Change history: Model rollout and config changes are recorded in our deployment audit trail, including operator identity, diff of configuration, and rollout window. We retain rollout artifacts tied to the release id."

Evidence bundle checklist (what to attach to e-mail when buyer asks for proof):
- Signed SOC2 summary + scope map (redacted as needed)
- ISO alignment statement or certificate snapshot if applicable
- BAA template and summary of controls mapped to HIPAA safeguards (if applicable)
- Sample audit-log export (sanitized) showing request id, timestamp, model version, and outcome
- Access matrix (roles and least-privilege mapping) and recent access-review proof (screenshot or export)
- Data retention policy excerpt and deletion log sample (sanitized)
- Network diagram showing tenancy/isolation boundaries for Dedicated and Private
- KMS/HSM architecture summary and key rotation cadence
- Incident response runbook excerpt and most recent tabletop test summary

Competitive notes (quick spicy takes for objection handling):
- Competitor A (managed endpoints): often claims a blanket SOC2 but scopes exclude cross-customer controls like request routing; emphasize Redwood’s scope map which ties controls to the inference plane customers use.
- Competitor B (self-hosted runtimes): good for control but lacks turnkey evidence packages and onboarding; highlight Redwood Private’s prebuilt artifact set + concierge onboarding.
- Competitor C (large cloud provider): broad compliance posture but limited model-level auditability; position Redwood as more transparent for model rollouts, audit logs, and per-request metadata.

Common security objections and scripts:
- "We need proof of isolation." -> "We will send the tenancy network diagram, isolation design note, and a sanitized audit log extract showing tenant-scoped requests. For immediate validation we can schedule a pre-PO security review with Solutions Eng."
- "What about logs containing PII/PHI?" -> "By default inference logs are minimally retained and can be filtered; for HIPAA customers we support Private deployments with tenant-level encryption and an option to disable retained logs entirely. We also offer a secure delivery pipeline to customer SIEM so logs never reside long-term in our hosted buckets."
- "Are your controls tester-friendly?" -> "Yes. We provide a controls map that maps our policies and artifacts to common frameworks (SOC2 criteria, ISO Annex A, HIPAA safeguards). We also provide scoped artifact exports for third-party auditors on NDA."

Operational playbook for evidence requests (step-by-step):
1) AE triages request, records RFI/Jira id and scope (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA).
2) AE tags CSE and Solutions Eng in the ticket, attaches the bundle checklist template.
3) Solutions Eng pulls sanitized audit-log sample and scope map; Security PM prepares control mapping.
4) Send zip with artifacts, include short README tying each item to RFI questions.
5) For deep technical review, offer a 60–90 minute meeting with Security + Solutions Eng.

Templates (copy/paste ready):
- Short reply for initial ask: "Thanks — we can provide a controls summary and sanitized evidence bundle. I’ve attached our SOC2 scope map and a sample audit-log extract. Would you like us to schedule a technical review with our Solutions team?"
- Follow-up with artifacts: "Attached: SOC2-summary.pdf, audit-log-sample.csv (sanitized), access-review-export.csv, BAA-template.pdf. See README.txt for mapping to your RFI questions. We can expand any item under NDA."

Open questions & next work items for GTM/security pairing:
- Create a standardized "sanitization rubric" for log samples so exports are consistent across deals.
- QoS: document expected SLAs for artifact delivery times (e.g., artifacts sent within 3 business days of request).
- Packaged demo for on-site/network architecture walkthrough for customers evaluating Private on-prem.

Appendix: quick references for AE/CSE
- Who to call: Solutions Eng escalation (oncall list), Security PM (Samira Patel), Legal for BAAs (Priya Shah).
- Slack channels: #sales-security, #solutions-escalations
- Typical artifacts file sizes and formats: PDF, CSV, PNG network diagram, Markdown README.

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Need to add the latest SOC2 2026 summary once signed off.
- Ask infra to generate a canonical sanitized audit log with multi-region examples.
